key_insight: Lower prediction error does not necessarily mean better physical fidelity: neural operators can score well on field error while misrepresenting flow fluctuation energy and related statistics.
engineering_relevance: For CFD surrogate models, benchmark accuracy should be paired with physics-aware diagnostics so engineers can judge whether a model preserves quantities that matter for design and analysis.
method: Paired CFD and PIV flow data around a NACA4418 airfoil were used to test neural-operator surrogates.
A mean-preserving input intervention removed velocity fluctuations from selected regions of observed flow histories.
An output attenuation stress test compared standard benchmark errors against domain-summed fluctuation-energy metrics.
evidence_signal: Across four neural operators, removing fluctuations from the most energetic 10% of valid observed cells changed forecasts more than equal-area random removal, and one CNO showed lower velocity-field error but higher two-component fluctuation-energy error on both analysis subsets.
watch_item: The fluctuation-removal masks were not matched for removed energy, so the sensitivity contrast is not proof of causal physical importance.
paper_title: Do Better Scores Mean Better Physics? Physics-Grounded Explanations for Sim2Real Neural Operators
